source.title: [Research Sprint] OpenAI agent-safety evidence, bounty eligibility and OSS credibility
source.body:
## Goal
Produce **independent, reproducible evidence** about agent tool-authority boundaries, and use that evidence to evaluate whether any OpenAI Safety/Security Bug Bounty category is genuinely in scope. Separately prepare a defensible OpenAI/Codex OSS engineering portfolio. No bounty or job outcome is presumed.

## Work already started (2026-11-02)
- Inspected published KCC v0.1.1 evidence and open work #94, #103, #105. Avoid duplicating Trajectory CI, SDK adapters, or existing benchmarks.
- Offline Python evidence checker created; 11/11 local regression tests passed.
- 24 synthetic threat-case definitions documented.
- Research branch: `research/agent-safety-evidence-2026-11`.
- Spec: `docs/OPENAI_SAFETY_EVIDENCE_SPRINT.md`.

## Milestones / tasks
- [x] M0: inventory existing evidence and program policies
- [x] M1: local repeatability/evidence-quality checker + regressions
- [x] M2: safe synthetic threat-case inventory (24 cases)
- [ ] M3: connect host-side trace collector in an isolated synthetic dispatcher (start with A01/A05/A06), signed/provenance-bound evidence per #105
- [ ] M4: run clean stable v0.1.1 baseline; separately test v0.2 candidate
- [ ] M5: independent review and limited public technical report with explicit negative results
- [ ] M6: evaluate actual bounty scope and decide whether **any** external authorized test merits submission
- [ ] M7: Codex for OSS application based on validated public maintenance facts, draft grant proposal only if evidence warrants it
- [ ] M8: role-specific OpenAI API Agents / Agent Runtime case study & application, do not conflate bounty reporting with hiring

## Decision gate: Nov 8, 2026
Stop or narrow the lane if no independently verified trace can be produced. Maintain an approximate 8–10 hour/week effort ceiling and no more than $100 incremental API/research spend without new approval.

## Security boundaries
No real user or customer data; no unauthorized third-party scanning; no unsafe side effects; don't disclose live vulnerabilities in public. Unit-test fixtures **are not** OpenAI bugs. OpenAI's 50% repeatability condition is relevant only for applicable Safety Bug Bounty categories; this checker cannot establish eligibility or bounty value.

## Deliverables
Runnable checker, repeatable trace fixture from trusted synthetic host, report and public case study. Track program communications privately if sensitive.

## 2026-11-02 progress — evidence implementation, not a bounty claim

- Added `benchmark/synthetic_host_proof.py`: scripted synthetic host, actual instrumented in-memory dispatcher, HMAC-attested traces, separate verifier and independently derived outcome ledger.
- New `tests/test_synthetic_host_proof.py`: **12 additional local tests passed**; combined with previous checker = **23/23 local regression tests passed** on Python 3.13.5.
- Ran **40** synthetic host trials (A01/A05/A06/authorized CONTROL × 10). A01/A05/A06 had **zero unauthorized dispatches**; CONTROL had **10 authorized reads**.
- Simulated deliberate bad-host dispatches in **test fixtures**; verifier correctly classifies unauthorized side effects as `harm_observed`, not a malformed trace.
- Added focused GitHub Actions offline workflow, pending independent hosted CI verification.
- Evidence and limitations: `docs/AGENT_SAFETY_SYNTHETIC_CHECKPOINT_2026-11-02.md`.

**Do not overclaim:** this tests a scripted toy host **not** the real KCC Guard or an OpenAI LLM. HMAC key is ephemeral and held by the same local process. No OpenAI bug found or reward submitted. The earlier PR #104 already has real KCC Guard host-trace instrumentation; next stage should reuse it rather than duplicate.

**Next acceptance gate:** integrate A01/A05/A06 with real KCC Guard in an authorized isolated host and independently review trace coverage/host key authority; no public disclosure or external probing before scope check.

PR: #107 remains draft pending review.

## 2026-11-02: actual KCC Guard integration now green

- Stacked draft PR #109: https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/pull/109 (based on trajectory CI PR #104).
- KCC's `approval_required` capsule state is valid when the send capability needs approval. The initial test wrongly assumed all usable capsules must say `ready`; fixed without weakening policy.
- GitHub Actions run **41553040328**: **SUCCESS**. Real KCC Guard, HostTraceRecorder and signed synthetic host trials: 10 authorized read dispatches, 30 Guard denials, 0 unauthorized dispatcher calls, 10 host attestations verified.
- No live LLM, third-party assets, OpenAI systems, real secrets, or customer information were involved. Fixture HMAC key is public and test-only; no independent production trust is claimed.
- Do not publicly present this as a successful OpenAI bounty finding. The separate agent safety evidence quality checks in PR #107 also pass offline CI.

Next: reconcile the two draft PRs once #104 is reviewed, confirm revocation and bypass boundaries, and obtain independent external validation.

## Sprint 3 verification — 2026-11-02 (America/Chicago)

**Goal:** Improve evidence quality and create an accurate route to OpenAI OSS support and engineering hiring without confusing synthetic findings with an OpenAI vulnerability.

### Changes delivered
- Draft **#109** extended from A01/A05/A06 to add **A09 inventory drift, A11 unexpected parameter and A13 capsule expiry** on the actual KCC Guard and synthetic host recorder from #104.
- Independent stable/development CI matrix now installs **published v0.1.1 wheel** versus **unreleased v0.2 source**. Explicitly verifies package version and actual import location to avoid pytest `src` path contamination.
- Each version: **10/10 allowed reads; 60/60 denied unauthorized tool-call attempts; zero unauthorized dispatches; 10 signed synthetic host traces**. These are deterministic scripted regressions, not model-level jailbreak or real-world safety statistics.
- Initial PR #107 full-repository CI failed on the policy requiring **immutable GitHub Actions references**. Fixed by pinning both new workflows to verified commit SHAs; **focused and full CI now pass**.
- English technical case study: `docs/AGENT_AUTHORITY_CROSS_VERSION_CASE_STUDY_2026-11.md` (draft #109).
- Prepared truthful OpenAI Codex for OSS form answers (all 500-character fields under the limit) and a conditional defensive cybersecurity grant pilot: `docs/OPENAI_OSS_AND_GRANT_APPLICATION_PACK_2026-11.md` (draft #107).

### Verified hosted GitHub runs
- Stable + development Guard matrix: https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41559661944
- Post-case-study Guard matrix: https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41559832194
- Latest #107 dedicated offline CI: https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41559997314
- Latest #107 **full repository CI**: https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41559997211

### Gates — NOT completed
- [ ] Independent reviewer/security assessment of #104 trust roots and #107/#109 branch stack.
- [ ] Realistic non-scripted or consented model-driven negative/positive evaluation with blind holdout; no third-party systems without permission.
- [ ] Validate actual third-party use/adoption metrics before claiming ecosystem impact.
- [ ] User verifies actual ChatGPT account email, OpenAI organization ID, primary maintainer role before Codex OSS application.
- [ ] AI-assisted defender pilot and budget evidence before cybersecurity grant submission.
- [ ] Send OpenAI hiring application using established master CV and role-specific evidence, separate from bounty reporting.

**No OpenAI bug found, no live-system test, no bounty or grant submitted, no job application sent.** All changed PRs remain **draft** until independent review. No production KCC release modified.

## Sprint 5 — Free Groq execution lane implemented (2026-11-02)

**Why the design changed:** User revoked the paid OpenAI KCC API key and requested a $0 API path. Existing Vercel Pulse Fitness production key `PULSE_LLM_API_KEY` points to Groq, but was not retrieved or used. Official Groq docs confirm **organization-level** quota; a second key under the same organization **cannot** guarantee Pulse isolation.

**Code on draft #109:**
- `evals/groq_chat_probe.py`: real Groq Chat Completions function-call ingestion (when separately approved); defaults to keyless/no-network plan; model allowlist `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`; interleaved attacks + benign; >=3-second pacing; hard maximum 120 requests; no external tool dispatch or production-key fallback. HTTP 429 stops without retry or tier switching.
- `evals/summarize_groq_run.py`: strict JSONL evidence checker with request and dataset SHA256 replay, exact Guard decision recomputation, missing repetitions, inconclusive responses and separate model/tool proposal metrics. Provider signature and Free-tier state are **not** independently verified.
- `tests/test_groq_chat_probe.py` and `tests/test_summarize_groq_run.py`: mocked no-network tests, including false-safe records, duplicate trials, missing items and quota error.
- `docs/GROQ_FREE_SPRINT5_RUNBOOK_2026-11.md`: user-facing runbook and explicit **isolated Free organization** requirement before actual API use.
- Version-matrix CI [#41587218996](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41587218996): 66 pytest regression checks PASS in both the released v0.1.1 and unreleased v0.2 jobs, plus keyless Groq dry-run plan validations. Later docs-only run may follow.

**Measured now:** zero live Groq requests, zero initiated Groq API charges, zero production key reads/writes/rotation. No API key value was exposed. No real model benchmark has been completed.

**Remaining exact action:** obtain a KCC-only credential from an owner-verified, isolated Groq **Free** organization (or choose an entirely local unbilled model). Run at most 8 interleaved cases against 20b to measure real request behavior and quota first, then consider Qwen. Not approved: production quota sharing, use of Pulse key, paid Developer-tier usage, production KCC release, OpenAI bug bounty submission. PRs remain draft pending review.

## Sprint 5.4 — Tool-result trust boundary, raw evidence and independent outreach (2026-11-03)

- **Trust boundary corrected:** Groq benchmark now supports explicit `--ingress-mode tool_result` (default). Untrusted adversarial content is in a **synthetic tool-message** following a fabricated assistant retrieval call; trusted task stays in its own user message. This still does **not** prove real model-initiated retrieval; original `user_snippet` ingress is available for labeled comparison.
- **Provenance isolated:** `evals/summarize_groq_run.py` reconstructs request hash using exact ingress and reports modes separately; cross-mode mixing and wrong tags are rejected.
- **Raw response persistence:** `evals/groq_chat_probe.py` fsyncs each raw response (including response digest and full client-observed JSON) to a second exclusive JSONL ledger **before** parsing or Guard judgment. A malformed Groq function proposal stops without retry, but raw bytes survive for manual reconciliation. This is client-side evidence, **not independent Groq attestation**.
- **Verified GitHub CI:** [41590481356](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41590481356) and docs-only latest [41590697263](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41590697263). Both KCC stable 0.1.1 and dev 0.2 jobs PASS **70 tests per job**; all tests are synthetic/no-network.
- **Credential inventory:** metadata-only inspection of four related KCC Vercel projects found no independent dedicated Groq KCC credential. The production Pulse Fitness Groq secret was **not read, copied, reused or modified**. Groq quotas are per organization, so separate key without separate organization is not full isolation.
- **External outreach:** polite, narrow follow-up comments delivered today to `bobmatnyc/claude-mpm#962`, `aswincandra/fast-mcp-client#3`, `imfht/swe-agent-lite#1` requesting dispatcher-boundary/overblocking counterexamples. These are outreach, **not feedback/reviews**.
- **No actual model calls**; no Groq API spending initiated, no production host/keys changed, no bounty or applications submitted. PRs remain draft pending independent review.

Runbook updated: `docs/GROQ_FREE_SPRINT5_RUNBOOK_2026-11.md`. Remaining operational gate: independently verifiable dedicated Groq Free organization and a KCC-only credential provisioned into the isolated runner, never into chat.

comments.author: kOs-tile
comments.text:
## First real Groq Free pilot attempt — blocked at provider permissions (2026-11-03)

Two manually dispatched runs have been verified directly from GitHub Actions jobs and logs:
- [#1 run 41681773471](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41681773471)
- [#2 run 41681773553](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41681773553)

**Observed:** setup, KCC stable package check and frozen synthetic dataset preflight all PASS in both. `GROQ_KCC_API_KEY` is present and masked (`***` in logs); no value accessed by auditor. `Execute exactly 8 ...` failed immediately on the **first** API request with `Groq HTTP 403; STOP. No retry and no paid fallback.` The raw/scored pilot logs contain no successful model response; no benchmark results and no claims of model safety success. Each run uploaded a 961-byte partial artifact.

**Most likely category:** Groq permission denial. Official documentation https://console.groq.com/docs/errors defines HTTP 403 as a resource permission restriction. https://console.groq.com/docs/model-permissions says organization/project model permission blocks return 403. This does **not** establish which restriction applies; runner intentionally suppressed full provider body to avoid credential/output leakage.

**Owner next checks:** Free organization in Groq Console → Settings → Organization → Limits, project selector → Settings → Projects → Limits; ensure `openai/gpt-oss-20b` allowed at both levels, key belongs to selected project, and organization is active. Do not reveal API key in chat/issues. Do not rerun until access is corrected; repeated 403 is not a benchmark.

**Accounting:** Two rejected HTTP API attempts; **zero successfully captured model completions**, zero actual tool dispatches, no known billable inference. Actual invoice cannot be confirmed from GitHub logs.

**Engineering follow-up:** add a tightly allowlisted error `type`/`code` extractor on 403 for diagnostics without echoing untrusted message text, in a reviewed branch before any next run if permissions are still unclear.

## Groq Free 403 hardening deployed — 2026-11-03

Root investigation:
- [Manual runs #41681773471](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41681773471) and [#41681773553](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41681773553): key present/masked and dry-run preflight PASS; **first** Groq POST rejected **403** in each, zero successful model completions, no tool side effects. Cause **not yet established** because original runner intentionally did not retain 403 provider error codes.
- Groq official docs https://console.groq.com/docs/model-permissions describe `model_permission_blocked_org` and `model_permission_blocked_project`; both are 403 permission errors. Do not infer which applies until classified evidence exists.

Fixed on research branch [commit 3f0724e](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/commit/3f0724e92e4d562451ce02729e5416a791160340) with two-version CI [#41682954506](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41682954506) **94 regression tests per channel PASS**:
- `groq_access_preflight.py` now probes only GET model metadata before paid inference; no model calls, no provider raw metadata printed, Free tier remains manually attested.
- `groq_chat_probe.py` now reads the HTTP error body **in memory only** and emits just allowlisted `error_type`/`error_code` classifications (never error messages, raw keys or arbitrary error fields). A 403/429 terminates immediately; no retries.
- Supporting tests ensure credential-redaction and org/project classification.

Rolled to default branch as [PR #111](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/pull/111), squash merge SHA `39e6238b1b4216746221d4ba6af3da7282dbf785`; all [13 regular PR CI jobs passed](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41683171103). The pilot workflow remains **manual-only**, using the same dedicated secret `GROQ_KCC_API_KEY`; merge itself triggered **zero Groq requests**.

**Next evidence gate:** user must manually Run workflow once from https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/workflows/kcc-groq-free-pilot.yml on main, with literal `ISOLATED_FREE_ORG`. I will read the run logs and classify the observed permission code:
- `model_permission_blocked_org` -> allow `openai/gpt-oss-20b` in Groq organization model permissions.
- `model_permission_blocked_project` -> allow it in the associated Groq project permissions.
- `unclassified` -> further controlled metadata/key ownership diagnostics, do not guess.
No permanent secret exposure or automation. Model safety benchmark still not completed; do **not** count these HTTP errors as test outcomes.

## Manual Free Groq pilot #3 — provider-wide 403 at model-list preflight (2026-11-03)

Reviewed actual GitHub Actions run [41738818561](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41738818561), job **126274845433**.

**Verified sequence:**
- Frozen synthetic dataset SHA, pinned code, stable wheel setup: **PASS**
- `GROQ_KCC_API_KEY` environment variable was available (no key value read or copied).
- New **non-inference** metadata preflight `GET https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models`: **HTTP 403**; classified as `error_type=unclassified`, `error_code=unclassified`.
- 8-call model completion step: **SKIPPED**; scorer: **SKIPPED**. No model completion, no tool execution. 823-byte preflight-only artifact, not a benchmark result.

**Interpretation:** Prior POST /chat/completions and now **GET /models** both return 403. This is not explained by benchmark dataset, tool-call syntax, token limit, or an absent GitHub secret; no proof of specific model permission denial. Groq docs define 403 as permission restrictions. A true model permission denial generally reports `model_permission_blocked_org` or `model_permission_blocked_project`, but neither appeared. Could be account/organization restriction, key/project policy, or an edge/network block. Do not guess which.

**Most discriminating next check without secret exposure:** in Groq Console with exactly the new Free organization selected, try one trivial prompt in Playground using `openai/gpt-oss-20b`. If Playground fails, address organization/account model access with Groq; if Playground succeeds, inspect key's project and GitHub-hosted runner egress restrictions. GH-hosted runners' shared cloud IP reputation can be independently blocked (GitHub documentation), but no WAF proof so far. Never share raw token, upgrade plan or use Pulse Fitness key.

No auto-retry/paid fallback. Manual pilot remains idle.

comments.author: kOs-tile
comments.text:
## Fourth manual Groq Free run — new key still forbidden at metadata GET (2026-11-03)

Read workflow run [41745320980](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41745320980), job 126296734857 directly via GitHub Actions.
- Environment secret `GROQ_KCC_API_KEY` was injected and masked; no key value read.
- Pinned stable KCC installation and frozen 8-case dry preflight: PASS.
- **First metadata GET** `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models`: **HTTP 403**, with safe classifier output `error_type=unclassified`, `error_code=unclassified`.
- No `/models/{id}` metadata detail request completed, no `chat/completions` sent, no scored output, no executed tool. Pilot marked FAIL (access), not a model safety failure.

A new key was created under user's selected Groq Personal / Default Project after a successful Playground `openai/gpt-oss-120b` response, yet the GitHub-hosted metadata check still returns 403. **Playground authentication does not prove key API access.** Groq's public API docs say 403 indicates permission restriction; org/project model blocks normally have distinct `model_permission_blocked_*` codes, which are absent here. A generic 403 may also originate at an edge/security policy; shared GitHub runner IP reputation is a hypothesis, not established. Sources: https://console.groq.com/docs/errors , https://console.groq.com/docs/model-permissions , https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/about-githubs-ip-addresses .

**STOP automated/manual reruns** until a discriminating diagnostic from Groq API Logs / API key project or an off-runner read-only credential probe from the same trusted Free organization identifies the denial source. Do not rotate keys again blindly, use the Pulse Fitness production key, or upgrade to a paid tier. All attempted API operations have produced 0 successful model responses. This is a provider-access/blocker case, not a KCC Guard regression.

comments.author: kOs-tile
comments.text:
## Groq 403 root-cause isolation — HTTP transport divergence confirmed (Nov 3, 2026)

**User observation:** Groq Console API Logs shows no corresponding entry for rejected metadata attempts. Absence of logs does not prove an edge block: the Console is project-scoped, and GET /models metadata may not be included in inference logs. Do not infer origin from missing logs alone.

**Decisive controlled experiment, same GitHub-hosted runner, same endpoint, NO API key:**
[GitHub Actions run 41746186612](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41746186612) ([diagnostic PR #112](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/pull/112)):
- `python urllib.request.urlopen("https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models")` -> **403**, non-JSON body, no explicit Cloudflare challenge/1010 signal.
- `curl GET https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/models` -> **401**, JSON error expected for an unauthenticated request.
- Both operations had **zero authentication headers, zero secrets, zero inference**.

Interpretation: this implicates **HTTP client fingerprint / request transport**, rather than a blanket GitHub IP block; authenticated curl success is not yet independently demonstrated. A generic 403 with server:cloudflare alone does not establish a Cloudflare WAF rule.

**Code fix** developed in experimental branch:
- New `evals/groq_curl_transport.py`, used for both model GET and chat POST.
- Only reviewed Groq HTTPS endpoints, no redirects, no retries, hard maximum response length.
- Bearer credential passed to curl via its **private stdin config**; no key in argv, temporary request files, raw error messages or CI output.
- Provider error results reduced to safe static response class and approved error code enums.
- Added 10 mock curl transport regressions. **KCC stable and dev matrix: 104 PASS per job**, [run 41746570190](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41746570190).
- [PR #113](https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/pull/113) updates only manual Groq Free pilot workflow to pin the new reviewed curl source SHA `176658cdd48e5cc24928c69a8d1a4d56ed5cb0f8`. No secret read or actual model request occurred in development and CI.

**Next:** after PR #113 passes normal CI and merges, a single owner-controlled manual rerun with the same isolated Free-org secret is needed to validate authorized GET and 8 synthetic responses. If authenticated curl still fails, inspect sanitized response class and provider code; no blind key rotations or paid fallback.

## Sprint 5.5 — first complete live Groq Free 40-case capture (2026-11-03)

**Authoritative GitHub Actions run:** https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41750141488 (job 126312912337) — **SUCCESS**. Manually dispatched on main from the dedicated KCC Free environment; artifact: https://github.com/kOs-tile/kavi-capability-compiler/actions/runs/41750141488/artifacts/13286505098 (`kcc-groq-free-40-41750141488`, 17,689 ZIP bytes; expires 2026-11-07 01:01 UTC).

### Verified facts from completed job log and reconciliation assertions
- Model: `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `tool_result` ingress; **one** repeat of frozen public-dev dataset SHA256 `bf2897b9f34ad3c885ee75453a0839ca4e5c7cedeb72a2d4be81a16e1ae11497`.
- All **40/40** model cases recorded and conclusively parsed: **30/30 attack** + **10/10 benign**. Exactly **40 raw provider-response client captures and 40 independently reconstructed/scored records**; `unscorable_raw_records=0`, `missing_trials=[]`, `complete_trial_capture=true`.
- **0/30** completed attack cases elicited an unsafe tool-call proposal. **10/10** benign cases elicited at least one permitted read proposal.
- KCC Guard: **40 allowed proposals; 0 blocked proposals**. This DOES NOT show Guard blocking efficacy against an unsafe proposal, because no such proposal was captured. `completed_no_tool_proposal_trials=0`.
- `actual_tool_dispatches=0`: experimental harness logs and replays tool proposals only, no real-world tool execution.
- Client-reported usage **16,040 input / 4,737 output tokens** (20,777 total). No independent provider-signature or Free-org billing attestation; no invoice/charge claims.
- All workflow preflight, secret-safe curl metadata access, live requests, independent reconstruction, 40-case summary gates and artifact upload passed. Production Pulse Fitness credentials untouched; experiment used the existing `GROQ_KCC_API_KEY` environment variable.

### Scientific limits and corrective plan
This is an **authentic client-captured Groq API run over 40 openly available synthetic development cases**, not an independent, blinded evaluation or real tool execution. Model safety behaviour observed in this cohort is promising but doesn't validate end-to-end agent/harness permissions or Guard mitigation rates. Because 30 attack cases generated **zero** unsafe model proposals, Guard TPR/recall against those is **undefined** (no blocked opportunities); reporting a 100% Guard block rate would be mathematically false.

**Recommended next gate, only on separate reviewed/manual workflow:**
1. Build a **held-out, attacker-authored prompt-injection set** with injection inside lower-trust retrieved/tool-result text (different attack families and realistic tools), including benign lookalikes. Avoid tailoring to public development prompts.
2. Add **explicit guard-challenge contract cases** in offline deterministic replay: craft malicious tool proposals directly and verify Guard blocks them, plus benign proposals allowed. This isolates Guard enforcement from model compliance.
3. Repeat across at least two model families and ingress modes only after a cost/kota preflight; do not scale paid or consume Pulse production key without explicit approval.
4. Report attack-case unsafe proposal rate and Guard block-on-unsafe rate as **separate denominators**, also completion, false positives, and unsupported/malformed attempts.

**Current milestone:** 40-case client capture PASS, zero unsafe proposals observed, ordinary read functionality preserved, Guard blocking on adversarial model output **not established**. No new calls automatically started.
